name: Joe Kent
role: Former director of the National Counterterrorism Center (July 2025 to March 2026; resigned over the Iran war); Republican nominee for Washington's 3rd congressional district in 2022 and 2024; retired Army Special Forces warrant officer and former CIA paramilitary officer
summary: Joe Kent is an America First Republican who combines strong opposition to foreign wars and nation building with strict immigration enforcement, gun rights, market and states-first approaches to health care and energy, and protectionist trade aimed at China. He is pro-life but leaves abortion to the states, opposes federal health care and climate programs, and attacks a 'ruling class'. In March 2026 he resigned as counterterrorism director, saying the Iran war was begun under pressure from Israel and its American lobby.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Says the nation must retain a modern, highly skilled military.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Pledges to fight any effort to defund the police and to keep criminals in prison.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says he is pro-life, believes life begins at conception and would always vote for life, with an exception where the mother's life is at risk; since Dobbs he leaves it to the states and opposes new federal legislation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Said in 2022 'we need to stop this out of control spending' that added trillions to the deficit, blamed printing money for inflation, and his platform calls for a balanced budget and ending needless spending.

ban-cartels.rationale: His platform says social media companies are monopolies that must be broken up, and in the debate he called for more competition against a few price-gouging health conglomerates.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He advocates Congress withholding the federal budget to compel changes in executive energy policy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Said in 2024 that legislation must end birthright citizenship, the ability to come here, have a child and have that child be a citizen.

close-ties-china.rationale: Calls the CCP the number one national security threat, wants it isolated, with tariffs, sanctions and a Pacific coalition against it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said in 2021 that the social contract is that 'we the people get to choose those who have power over us' and that officials who ignore this should lose power.

corporate-influence.rationale: Names the governing class 'and their corporate counterparts' as not serving workers and says politicians get bought by donors and the military-industrial complex.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He explicitly supports a social fallback system and continued Medicare, Medicaid and veterans’ benefits.

decide-locally.rationale: Repeatedly says decisions belong to states and counties: 'Washingtonians should make policy for Washington State', logging and nuclear plants for states and localities, curriculum back to the states, abortion left to the states.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In the 2022 debate he said climate has always changed, that carbon as the cause 'is not definitive', and that the US should stay out of the Paris accord and anything from the UN that limits energy independence.

elite-replacement.rationale: Said 'the administration is trying to replace' American citizens through immigration (guides.vote summary of his statements, 2024). Low because it is a secondhand summary and names the administration rather than elites.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mixed: wants troops out of Iraq, Syria and Afghanistan and criticises the US as security guarantor of Europe, but the 2022 platform says to strengthen NATO with burden sharing.

exclude-trans-women-women-only-spaces.rationale: At a 2024 town hall he said, as reported, that he opposes letting biological males compete against females or enter girls' locker rooms. Reported, not his own text, and it covers sports and locker rooms only.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In the 2022 debate: 'turn back on U.S. energy 100 percent, especially our fossil fuels', restore Keystone XL and exploratory drilling permits; platform lists natural gas and oil in an all-of-the-above strategy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Platform: accelerate development of clean and safe breakthrough nuclear reactor technology; in the 2022 debate 'we need to pursue nuclear'.

free-trade.rationale: Calls for a protectionist trade policy, tariffs, and a ban on offshoring by US companies, which rejects the claim that free trade benefits everyone.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Criticised his opponent for backing biological men in girls' bathrooms and sports and opposed medical transition for minors.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Said in 2024 that saying 'a boy's not a girl, a girl's not a boy' is part of a push to control language and attacked gender-affirming care for minors and biological men in girls' spaces.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: In the 2022 OPB debate he said the earth is in a heating cycle but that it is not definitive that carbon causes it; he doubts, without flatly denying, human causation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Agreed with a host's proposal to 'privatize' Social Security for younger workers through individual savings accounts (Lars Larson Show, 2022), while saying retirees and those near retirement would not change. Limited to younger workers, hence medium.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Says marijuana conviction policy is 'a states' issue' and supports Washington state legalization but not federal legalization. Mixed.

limit-guns.rationale: Says he does not support any new gun legislation, opposes any effort to further restrict firearm ownership and backs constitutional carry and nationwide concealed-carry reciprocity.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: In the 2022 debate he attacked the repeal of the 'three strikes and you're out' law, which fixes sentences for repeat offenders, and asked his opponent to commit to keeping criminals in prison.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says the free market should be left to compete on energy and wants competition and deregulation in health care, but also backs a protectionist trade policy, tariffs and onshoring; the evidence is mixed, so low.

military-superiority.rationale: Platform: retain a modern, highly skilled military 'poised to strike and deter our enemies around the world at a moment's notice' and pivot to fighting China in every warfare domain.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He favors public funding that patients use among competing healthcare providers, including more veterans’ choice.

nation-first.rationale: Platform: 'Putting this nation first will always be my guiding principle when dealing with issues abroad'; survey names America First as the key principle. He still favours alliances and coalitions.

national-mission.rationale: Mocks the idea of spreading democracy 'through the barrel of a gun' as neocon nonsense and says the US must break the habit of nation building and toppling regimes.

open-borders.rationale: Calls for a border wall, no pathway to citizenship for illegal entrants, mass deportation and employer enforcement; calls the open border an invasion.

participatory-democracy.rationale: At 14:24–14:55 with Tim Pool he urges parents to attend school boards and hold institutions accountable even after homeschooling.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes a ruling or governing class that serves itself and China, calls for ending the career political class, and says politicians get bought by donors and the military-industrial complex.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He proposes expanding the child tax credit so families can support children.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Asked specifically about speech criticizing religion, he favors constitutional free speech over religious restrictions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Platform: strict immigration control; in 2022 he wanted to end economic immigration and visas that take jobs, saying H-1B labour depresses wages; in 2024 he said all illegal immigrants should be deported.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: On logging in the 2022 debate he said the funds generated in Skamania, Clark and Lewis counties, 'the vast majority of it, should stay there in those counties'. Stated for timber receipts specifically.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed: wants deregulation of health care, logging and fishing and says social media companies should be broken up; also wants a federal cap on drug prices. Points both ways.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: In December 2025 he contrasts American freedom to criticize religion with Sharia restrictions and praises the former.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Criticises foreign aid as money sent overseas while the American people come last; wants resources redirected to Americans.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said in 2024 'I don't care who you marry. I'm not gonna pass laws about that', treating it as not an issue for legislation; he did not give a stronger endorsement.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Speaks of 'biological men' and says 'a boy's not a girl', treating sex as a fixed biological category.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Opposes further firearm restrictions and said 'the American people should have the exact same weapons that our military has'. This reads against disarming citizens.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Called President Biden's loan forgiveness plan 'a complete disgrace & abuse of power' and opposes student loan forgiveness.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said in 2022 'we need to actually have a protectionist trade policy' with firms 'tariffed into nonexistence' if they do not build in America, and his platform strongly supports Trump's tariffs and offensive tariffs on Chinese imports.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His platform pledges to lower individual and corporate federal income taxes and says the government overtaxes; he states no support for higher taxes on high earners, and his stated direction is the opposite.

term-limits.rationale: Wants 8-year term limits for the House and Senate and says Congress should have limits mirroring the presidency.

traditional-family.rationale: Said in 2024 that the nuclear family is 'the real center of power' and that opponents are at war with it by breaking it up.

unions-good.rationale: Opposes the PRO Act, saying it 'forces workers to join unions', and called teachers' union leaders 'thugs'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In the debate he rejects a federal public option but welcomes state provision and publicly funded access through competing providers.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Backs presidential term limits as the model for Congress ('mirror the limits placed on the President').

voter-id.rationale: Said in 2022: 'We need to get back to voting in person, on a paper ballot, with an ID card that proves you're an eligible voter.'

notes:
Living: true per Wikipedia (no death recorded; still giving interviews in 2026). Positions are mainly from his 2022 platform, 2022 OPB answers and debate, a 2024 long-form interview, and 2026 statements. Joekentforcongress.com was read through the Internet Archive; joekent.com is a different person. Abortion: he once backed a federal ban (per Wikipedia) but his most recent position is states decide and no new federal law, while remaining pro-life; answered -2 on legality. Not answered because no clear position of his was found: minimum wage, unions, welfare, drugs, sex work, death penalty, surveillance, Israel statehood or aid, Ukraine borders, civil-liberties statements (his general free speech principle does not answer hate speech or media control), COVID and Fauci items (no matching statement). The Daily Chronicle reported he appeared to agree with a 'demographic replacement' question at a 2022 town hall, which his attorney disputed; the article was paywalled, so elite-replacement and ethnic-nation statements stay null. Reports of 2022 interviews with American Virtue and of a 2022 immigration moratorium were not read in primary form and are not used. Many 2026 interviews (Tucker Carlson, Shawn Ryan, Megyn Kelly, Breaking Points) focus on Iran and Israel and mostly do not match any statement. The hearing transcript was auto-captioned and mostly concerns the Signal chat, January 6 and the border.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 8 answers taken from it, 19 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Known answers are limited to sourced statements. Most campaign quotations come from an undated third-party compilation (guides.vote) and are marked low or medium where undated. The joekent.com and joekentforcongress.com campaign sites and the Washington State Standard and KGW debate coverage could not be opened (not found or HTTP 403). The Senate hearing transcript and the full resignation letter were not reachable. Kent's 2026 Shawn Ryan transcript is an unofficial repost; the full text was not read past the first 100,000 characters. Contested points: his claims about Israel, the Jan. 6 'political prisoners' framing, and the 2024 abortion position.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 10 answers taken from it, 14 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third pass; existing answers were not copied. All 490 statements and the existing blank list were checked against saved sources. Main effort covered the table and thin culture/means/globalism themes. No evidence established the listed Marxist doctrines, communal land tenure, atheistic schooling or a third economic system; opposition to Democrats is not evidence on one-party ideological rule. Cross-party cooperation against one war does not establish that all left/right distinctions are obsolete. The culture-war interview supports school-board participation, not armed revolution or rejecting elections. His memorial advocacy honors sacrifice but does not call the dead saints or assert that war improves national character. December 2025 comments address civic allegiance and speech restrictions, not the incompatibility of every Muslim or a general ethnic-state doctrine. The post-hearing PDF was accessible through web extraction but blocked on direct download; it was not used for answers. Confirmation evidence is restricted to Mr. Kent, excluding Messrs. Lukas and Eisenberg. Campaign-era healthcare and policing evidence is qualified; generic anti-government language is not converted into anarchism or class-instrument doctrine. Living person: zero inferred answers. Every non-null answer cites source text saved in this folder.

claude-sonnet-5-5 later pass (2026-11-19): re-read the Senate hearing, OPB answers and debate, the UnHerd, Tucker Carlson, Diesen and Shawn Ryan transcripts, Axios, Daily Signal, the Washington State Standard 2024 town-hall report and Racket News. Themes searched: economy, taxes, trade, energy and climate, healthcare, elections, immigration and border, guns, abortion, trans issues, Ukraine, Iran, Israel, China, crime. Two answers added for statements that did not exist in the earlier passes; no earlier answer changed. Kent's remark that he would use the military at the border does not state turning migrants back, so turn-back-illegal-migrants stays null. Taxes and social policy: he called them down-ballot issues and gave no position.
